name: Marine Corps waist-to-height ratio

source.document: MARADMIN 066/26, Change 1 to the Advance Notification of Changes to the Marine Corps Physical Fitness Test and Body Composition Evaluation Process (paragraphs 2, 3.d and 6)

ifOver: A body fat evaluation follows (the multi-site tape test or a BIA scale; the standard body fat limits are those of MCO 6110.3A, which we do not have). Marines whose PFT and CFT scores are 285 or higher are allowed up to 26% body fat (men) and 36% (women); 250 or higher adds 1 percentage point to the usual limit. A Marine over the limit by both methods goes to the Body Composition Program.
notes: The text says below 0.52, but the order's own maximum-waist table allows a ratio of exactly 0.52 (for example a 32.5 in waist at 62.5 in height), so the tool follows the table.
The waist is measured at the navel, twice, and the lower value is used. Waist and height are rounded down to 1/2 inch.
The standard is the same for every sex. Weight is still recorded in 2026 but is not used for the evaluation.
